name: Metaprogramming preserves the semantics owned by earlier chapters

input.fixture_ref: Compare ordinary dispatch, Method identity, Contract algebra, async scheduling, native handles, tokens and serialization before and after loading the META subsystem.

applicability.reason: Requires package metadata and decorator resolution. Re-probed: the old reason's claim that `include`, `@decorator` and capability forms are all parse diagnostics is partly stale. Module composition works through the `class A mixin M { }` HEADER form and a composed Module Method dispatches; `include` is simply not the v1 spelling. Decorators parse and reach the runtime but are never resolved, as META-V930 records. What this row still waits on is package metadata plus that decorator resolution, since it compares every earlier-chapter observable BEFORE and AFTER loading them.

expect.status: Every earlier chapter-owned observable is unchanged by loading Modules, package metadata, decorators, capabilities and reflection.
